safety_lines: In an emergency, call 999. For advice, call 111 or ask your pharmacist or GP.

facts.dose: TWO puffs when needed for wheeze or breathlessness
warnings: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working.
Do not use more often than advised.
get_help: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of the face or lips.

conflicts.label: TWO puffs when needed for wheeze or breathlessness
conflicts.leaflet: Usual dose: ONE puff when needed. Adults may take up to 2 puffs if needed.

conflicts.label: Maximum 4 times in 24 hours
conflicts.leaflet: When needed. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.

steps.text: Use 2 puffs when you wheeze or feel short of breath. This is what your label says.
steps.text_en: Use 2 puffs when you wheeze or feel short of breath. This is what your label says.
steps.picture_prompt: A person sitting calmly holding a blue inhaler with a spacer, one hand on their chest
steps.say: Use 2 puffs when you wheeze or feel short of breath. This is what your label says.

steps.text: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
steps.text_en: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist.
steps.picture_prompt: a person holding a medicine box and a leaflet, looking unsure
steps.say: Your label and leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist. Take care with this one.

steps.text: Shake your inhaler. Fit it into your spacer.
steps.text_en: Shake your inhaler. Fit it into your spacer.
steps.picture_prompt: Hands shaking an inhaler, then pushing the inhaler into the end of a clear plastic spacer tube
steps.say: Shake your inhaler. Fit it into your spacer. Take your time.

steps.text: Put the spacer mouthpiece in your mouth. Close your lips around it.
steps.text_en: Put the spacer mouthpiece in your mouth. Close your lips around it.
steps.picture_prompt: Side view of a person with lips closed around the mouthpiece of a clear spacer
steps.say: Put the spacer mouthpiece in your mouth. Close your lips around it. Take your time.

steps.text: Press the inhaler once. Breathe in slowly through your mouth. Repeat for your second puff.
steps.text_en: Press the inhaler once. Breathe in slowly through your mouth. Repeat for your second puff.
steps.picture_prompt: A person pressing the top of an inhaler with a finger while breathing in, with a soft arrow showing air going into the mouth
steps.say: Press the inhaler once. Breathe in slowly through your mouth. Repeat for your second puff. Take your time.

steps.text: Use your inhaler 4 times at most in 24 hours. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
steps.text_en: Use your inhaler 4 times at most in 24 hours. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours.
steps.picture_prompt: A clock face showing a full day, with four small inhaler icons around it and a red stop hand
steps.say: Use your inhaler 4 times at most in 24 hours. Do not take more than 8 puffs in 24 hours. Take care with this one.

steps.text: Your label and your leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist which is right.
steps.text_en: Your label and your leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist which is right.
steps.picture_prompt: A person at a pharmacy counter holding an inhaler box and a folded leaflet, talking to a pharmacist
steps.say: Your label and your leaflet say different things. Ask your pharmacist which is right. Take care with this one.

steps.text: Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working. Do not use your inhaler more often than advised.
steps.text_en: Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working. Do not use your inhaler more often than advised.
steps.picture_prompt: A person talking to a doctor in a small clinic room, holding an inhaler
steps.say: Tell your doctor if your usual dose stops working. Do not use your inhaler more often than advised. Take care with this one.

steps.text: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of your face or lips.
steps.text_en: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of your face or lips.
steps.picture_prompt: A person holding a phone to their ear, looking worried, with one hand on their chest and a slightly swollen face
steps.say: Call 999 if you have severe difficulty breathing or swelling of your face or lips.
